mainTopic: Being alone (יחוד) with גוים: the concern of עריות for a woman, and safety rules against שפיכות דמים for a man traveling with a גוי
overview: This amud first settles which case the משנה means when it forbids a woman from being alone with גוים. It is a case of three גוים where the man's wife is also there, because a Jew's wife guards him but a גוי's wife does not. The גמרא then asks why the משנה gives עריות as the reason and not the danger of שפיכות דמים. רבי ירמיה answers that she is an important woman whom they are afraid to kill. רב אידי answers that a woman's being a woman protects her from being killed. The גמרא shows where these two answers differ, and brings a ברייתא that supports רב אידי. Next it turns to a man alone with גוים and gives safety rules for traveling with one: which side to keep him on, staying higher on a slope, and naming a farther destination. That last rule is learned from יעקב and עשו and shown in a story about רבי עקיבא's students. A new story about רב מנשה begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about three גוים
steps.stepSummary: After earlier attempts (one or two גוים) did not work, the גמרא proposes that the משנה means a woman alone with three גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה means a case of three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a new way to read the משנה: the woman is alone with three גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule has to teach something special about גוים. A case that is forbidden even with Jews would teach nothing new. So the גמרא moves to a bigger group, three, hoping that this case is forbidden only with גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces a new suggestion after an earlier one failed)

steps.confusionAlert: This line answers a question from just before this section. The גמרא was asking what number of גוים the משנה means, and smaller numbers had already been ruled out.

phrases.english: Rather, [the mishnah is speaking] of three.
phrases.notes: He means the woman is alone with three גוים. Smaller numbers were already tried and turned down just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up from earlier attempts (before this section) to define the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might refer to one or two גוים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to three גוים.

steps.title: Even with Jews of loose morals, three would not be allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that with immoral Jews (פרוצים) even ten men are forbidden. So the case of three would not be special to גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take the matching case with Jews: would it be allowed with immoral Jews? But we learned in a משנה: 'One woman may be alone with two men.' And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: this was taught only about decent men. With immoral men, even ten is not allowed. There was an incident where ten men carried a woman out on a bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'three' answer. Since גוים are assumed to be immoral, the fair comparison is with immoral Jews, and with them even ten men are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in קידושין allows a woman to be with two men, but שמואל limits that to decent men. With פרוצים, there is no safety in numbers at all, as shown by the story of ten men who carried a woman away. So three גוים would teach nothing new compared with three immoral Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: people known to be immoral, loose in matters of עריות

phrases.english: The matching case regarding Jews:
with immoral people, is it permitted?
phrases.notes: The comparison is to immoral Jews, since גוים are assumed to be loose in these matters.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: 'But one woman'
may be alone with two men,'
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in קידושין 80b.

phrases.english: and Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only regarding decent men,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּפְרוּצִים אֲפִילּוּ עֲשָׂרָה נָמֵי לָא.
phrases.english: but with immoral men, even ten is also not [allowed].
There was an incident, and ten carried her out on a bier!
phrases.notes: They carried her out as if she were dead, so ten men together were no protection at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְוָותַהּ גַּבֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל, בִּפְרוּצִים מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה refers to three גוים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With immoral Jews even ten are forbidden, so three גוים would not be a rule special to גוים.

steps.title: The case is when his wife is with him
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a case where the man's wife is present. A Jew's wife guards him, but a גוי's wife does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is needed for a case where his wife is with him. A גוי's wife does not guard him, but a Jew's wife does guard him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by making the case of the משנה more specific: the man's wife is there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a Jew, his wife's presence is enough to keep him from sinning, so יחוד would be allowed. With a גוי, the wife's presence does not hold him back. This finally gives the משנה a rule that is special to גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed (for this specific case)
when his wife is with him

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ban on יחוד with גוים teaches something new in the case where the man's wife is present. A Jew's wife protects against sin, but a גוי's wife does not.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where his wife is with him.
A gentile, his wife does not guard him,
but a Jew, his wife guards him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a plain number of גוים, which would be no different from immoral Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a גוי whose wife is present, a case that would be allowed with a Jew.

steps.title: Why not forbid it because of murder?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה gives עריות as the reason, when it could have given the danger of שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him derive it because of bloodshed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Why does the משנה say the problem is עריות, when the danger of being killed would be an even more obvious reason?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right near our משנה, גוים are described as suspected of murder. If so, a woman alone with them should be forbidden simply because of danger to her life. Mentioning עריות seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: let him derive it (from a different reason)

phrases.english: And let him derive it because of bloodshed!
phrases.notes: In other words, why not forbid her being alone with them out of fear they will kill her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the reason the משנה gives.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice of עריות as the reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גוים are also suspected of murder, which would be a simpler reason to forbid יחוד.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: an important woman they fear to kill
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the משנה is talking about an important woman. They are afraid to kill her, so only the עריות concern remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: We are dealing with an important woman, whom they are afraid of.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives the first answer: the woman is important, so the גוים would not dare kill her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Murder is not a worry here because killing a woman of status would bring consequences the גוים fear. But her status does not stop them from sinning with her. So עריות is the only reason left.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
We are dealing with an important woman,
whom they are afraid of.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: בְּאִשָּׁה חֲשׁוּבָה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific kind of woman
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any woman alone with גוים is in danger of murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: An important woman is safe from murder, so only עריות is relevant.

steps.title: רב אידי: a woman carries her own protection
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי answers that a woman generally is not killed, since the גוים want her for עריות. Her being a woman is her protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי said: A woman has her weapons on her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי gives a second, more general answer to the murder question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אידי does not limit the case to an important woman. In his view, any woman is protected from murder because the גוים would want her for עריות rather than kill her. That is why the only concern the משנה mentions is עריות.

phrases.english: Rav Idi said:
A woman, her weapons are upon her.
phrases.notes: He means the fact that she is a woman is what saves her: they want her, so they won't kill her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אִידִי אָמַר: אִשָּׁה כְּלֵי זַיְינָהּ עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 4, parallel to רבי ירמיה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General reasoning about why murder is not the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A woman alone with גוים is in danger of murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any woman is protected from murder by her being a woman, so the issue is only עריות.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two answers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical case where the answers of רבי ירמיה and רב אידי would lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking where the two answers would actually give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers explain why murder is not mentioned. So the גמרא wants a case where they disagree in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is [the difference] between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between רבי ירמיה and רב אידי.

steps.title: An important woman who is not attractive
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a woman who is important among men but not attractive among women.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a woman who is important among men, but is not considered attractive among women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two views split over a woman who has status but is not attractive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי ירמיה, her importance protects her from murder. A common way to explain רב אידי is that her protection comes from being desirable, which this woman lacks, so the murder concern would return. The two answers therefore lead to different conclusions for her.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה: an important woman is safe from murder because of her status. רב אידי: a woman is safe because she is desirable. They differ over an important woman who is not attractive.

phrases.english: There is [a difference] between them:
a woman who is important among men,
but who is not important among the women.
phrases.notes: This means she is not considered attractive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ: אִשָּׁה חֲשׁוּבָה בֵּין אֲנָשִׁים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ over a woman who is important among men but unattractive among women.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב אידי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a woman is protected from being killed but still may not be alone with גוים because of עריות. This matches רב אידי בר אבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רב אידי בר אבין: a woman, even though she is safe from being killed, may not be alone with them, because they are suspected of forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב אידי's answer from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אידי said every woman is safe from being killed, because the גוים want her for עריות. The ברייתא speaks about any woman, not only an important one, and says 'peace is with her.' That fits רב אידי's view that her protection comes from being a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with his view (a support)
Literally 'peace is with her': she is safe from being killed
She may not be alone (in seclusion)

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא backs up רב אידי: any woman is safe from being killed, but she still may not be alone with גוים because of עריות.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Idi bar Avin:
phrases.notes: This is the same רב אידי from step 6, who said a woman's being a woman protects her.

phrases.aramaic: הָאִשָּׁה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַשָּׁלוֹם עִמָּהּ,
phrases.english: A woman, even though peace is with her,
phrases.notes: 'Peace is with her' means she is safe. They won't kill her.

phrases.english: may not be alone with them,
because they are suspected of forbidden relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the practical difference was found in step 8, a ברייתא is brought that supports רב אידי's side.
steps.raayaObject: רב אידי's claim that every woman is protected from being killed because of her being a woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says about any woman: 'peace is with her,' and only the עריות concern remains.

steps.title: Keep a traveling companion on your right side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Then a ברייתא says a Jew walking with a גוי should keep him on his right side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a person may not be alone with them. The Rabbis taught: a Jew who meets a גוי on the road should keep him on his right side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about a man being alone with גוים, and brings a ברייתא with practical safety rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern for a man is שפיכות דמים, the danger of being killed. If the גוי walks on the Jew's right, the Jew's stronger hand is close to him, so he can defend himself if attacked.

keyTerms.meaning: A person may not be alone with them
He positions him / keeps him at his side

phrases.english: A person may not be alone with them.
The Rabbis taught:
A Jew who happens to meet a gentile on the road —
keeps him at his right side.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יִתְיַיחֵד אָדָם עִמָּהֶן. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the משנה's rule about a man being alone with גוים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew walking with a גוי keeps him on his right side, so he can protect himself.

steps.title: It depends on what weapon he carries
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says the side depends on the weapon: with a sword keep him on the right, with a stick keep him on the left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: if he has a sword, keep him on your right. If he has a stick, keep him on your left.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different rule. He says the side you put the גוי on depends on which weapon he is carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gives one rule for every case. רבי ישמעאל says to look at the weapon. A sword is usually worn on the left side, and a stick is usually held in the right hand. So the Jew walks on the side where the weapon is, to keep him from using it easily.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
With a sword — he keeps him at his right,
with a stick — he keeps him at his left.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same ברייתא that disagrees with the single rule of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the גוי has a sword, keep him on the right. If he has a stick, keep him on the left.

steps.title: Stay higher on a slope and don't bend down
steps.stepSummary: On a hill, going up or down, the Jew should be above and the גוי below. The Jew also should not bend down in front of him, so his skull is not smashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were going up a hill or down a slope, the Jew should not be below with the גוי above. The Jew should be above and the גוי below. And he should not bend down in front of him, in case the גוי smashes his skull.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with more safety rules for walking with a גוי: where to stand on a slope, and not to bend down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone higher up has the advantage in a fight. So the Jew should never let the גוי be above him. Bending down puts his head at the attacker's mercy, so he should avoid that too.

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ עוֹלִין בְּמַעֲלֶה אוֹ יוֹרְדִין בִּירִידָה,
phrases.english: If they were going up an incline or going down a slope,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַטָּה וְגוֹי לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: the Jew should not be below with the gentile above,
rather the Jew above and the gentile below,
and he should not bend down in front of him,
in case he smashes his skull.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ עוֹלִין בְּמַעֲלֶה אוֹ יוֹרְדִין בִּירִידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with more safety rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a slope the Jew stays higher than the גוי, and he does not bend down in front of him.

steps.title: Name a farther destination
steps.stepSummary: If the גוי asks where the Jew is going, the Jew should name a place farther than his real destination.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he asks him where he is going, he should make the road longer for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives one more safety rule: what to answer when the גוי asks about your destination.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גוי thinks the Jew is going farther, he may plan to attack him later on the road. Then the Jew reaches his real stop and gets away before anything happens.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'widen the road': name a farther place

phrases.english: If he asked him where he is going —
he should make the road longer for him,
phrases.notes: He names a place past where he is really going.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another safety rule in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When asked about his destination, the Jew names a farther place.

steps.title: יעקב did this with עשו
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports the rule from יעקב אבינו, who told עשו he would meet him in שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is just what יעקב אבינו did with עשו the wicked, as it says: 'until I come to my lord to שעיר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to show that naming a farther destination is an old practice, going back to יעקב אבינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב told עשו he would come to him in שעיר, which made his route sound longer. Since this comes from the אבות, it shows the advice is proper and wise. The גמרא will look more closely at this פסוק next.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לְעֵשָׂו הָרָשָׁע,
phrases.english: the way our father Jacob did to Esau the wicked,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״עַד אֲשֶׁר אָבֹא אֶל אֲדֹנִי שֵׂעִירָה״,
phrases.english: as it is written: "until I come to my lord to Seir",

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לְעֵשָׂו הָרָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from the פסוק for the rule in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The rule to name a farther destination when a גוי asks where you are going.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 33:14, where יעקב tells עשו he will come to him in שעיר.

steps.title: יעקב actually went to סוכות, not שעיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the proof from יעקב: he told עשו he was going to שעיר, but the פסוק shows he really went to סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: "And יעקב traveled to סוכות."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק to finish the proof from step 14. יעקב said he would go to שעיר, but this פסוק shows he really went to סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needs both פסוקים together. The first shows what יעקב told עשו (שעיר, far away). The second shows where he really went (סוכות, closer). So יעקב named a farther place than his real destination, which is exactly the rule from step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written (introduces a פסוק)
to סוכות, the place יעקב really went

phrases.english: And it is written: "And Yaakov traveled to Sukkos."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 14 by showing יעקב's real destination.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a Jew should name a destination farther than his real one (step 13).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two פסוקים together: יעקב told עשו "שעיר" (בראשית 33:14), but actually traveled to סוכות (בראשית 33:17).

steps.title: The students of רבי עקיבא fool the bandits
steps.stepSummary: The students of רבי עקיבא, traveling to כזיב, told bandits they were going to עכו. When they reached כזיב they split off, and the bandits praised רבי עקיבא and his students.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, the students of רבי עקיבא were traveling to כזיב. Bandits met them and asked where they were going. They answered, "To עכו." When they reached כזיב, they separated from the bandits. The bandits asked, "Whose students are you?" They said, "Students of רבי עקיבא." The bandits said, "Fortunate are רבי עקיבא and his students, for no evil person has ever harmed them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a true story that shows the rule in action. The students named a farther city, so they escaped the bandits safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bandits thought they had plenty of time to attack before the students reached עכו. But the students' real stop was כזיב, the nearer city, so they slipped away first. Even the bandits admitted this was smart, which shows the advice really works.

keyTerms.meaning: the city the students were really going to
the farther city they told the bandits

steps.whatToRemember: Naming a farther destination protects you: the attacker waits, thinking he has time, and you reach your real stop first. The גמרא proves this from יעקב and shows it in the story of רבי עקיבא's students.

phrases.english: There was an incident with the students of Rabbi Akiva
who were traveling to Keziv;
bandits came upon them.
They said to them: Where are you going?
They said to them: To Akko.
phrases.notes: The students named a farther city, just like the rule in step 13.

phrases.english: Once they reached Keziv, they separated.
They said to them: Whose students are you?
They said to them: Students of Rabbi Akiva.
